title: Yeasty Chewy Irish Apple Crumble
description: Moist and delicious Irish apple crumble made with dehydrated Bramley apples and a hint of yeast for a chewy twist.

ingredients.name: Bramley apples
ingredients.notes: Dehydrate in a low-temperature oven (200°F) for 2 hours to remove excess moisture

ingredients.name: Baking powder
ingredients.notes: Active dry yeast (1 tsp) can be used as a substitute for a yeastier flavor

instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the dehydrated apples, granulated sugar, and a pinch of cinnamon. Mix well until the apples are evenly coated with the sugar and cinnamon mixture.
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and a pinch of nutmeg. Mix well until the dry ingredients are evenly combined.
Add the unsalted butter to the dry ingredients and use a pastry blender or your fingers to work the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the egg (if using) and vanilla extract to the flour mixture and mix until the dough comes together in a ball.
Press the dough evenly into the bottom of a 9x9-inch baking dish.
Add the apple mixture to the dough and mix until the apples are evenly distributed throughout the dough.
Top the apple mixture with the remaining dough, spreading it evenly to cover the entire surface.
Bake the crumble in the preheated oven for 35-40 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the apples are tender.
Remove the crumble from the oven and let it cool for 10-15 minutes before serving.
